dimensions.reasons: The author final image (.eval_workspace/exports/temple_courtyard_dusk.png) clearly depicts a traditional temple courtyard: a red-columned, two-storey main hall terminates a paved central court beneath golden upturned roofs. The pavilion, perimeter structures, trees, lantern frame, central bronze object, stairs, and entry-side statues establish a recognizable temple setting.
issues: The requested bronze bell reads as a squat bowl-shaped incense burner/cauldron on legs rather than a bell.
The gateway guardians do not convincingly read as stone lions.
The final camera is essentially centered and frontal rather than distinctly angled inward from the gateway.
The image is much darker and less open at its side and rear spaces than the bright, open courtyard requested.

dimensions.reasons: The hall columns, pavilion posts, lantern rack, stairs, plinths, paving, and roof structures generally have visible bases and credible connections in Group A wide views. The central vessel and its pedestal are also visibly grounded.
issues: The two guardian figures in the author final are made of visibly intersecting, stacked rounded pieces rather than coherent sculptural forms.
Group A detail_hall.png shows a narrow slanted gray strip and gold sphere near the porch with no clear purpose or convincing attachment.
Some beam-bracket and roof-edge components appear mechanically blocky or lightly intersecting.

dimensions.reasons: The main hall has an effective Chinese-inspired silhouette, with saturated red cylindrical columns, red-and-gold lattice panels, gray bracket bands, and broad gold-brown swept roofs. The upturned eaves are particularly clear in Group A wide_gateway.png and the author final.
issues: The guardian lions have indistinct, lumpy silhouettes and cannot confidently be identified as lions.
The bronze centerpiece does not have the silhouette of the requested bell.
The hanging lanterns render pink/salmon rather than the requested red.
Several decorative elements, including the unexplained gray roof/porch pieces, look like simple placeholder geometry.

dimensions.reasons: The scene is cleanly rendered and coherent as a stylized low-poly temple environment, with readable architectural layers, paving, shrubs, and strong silhouettes. The author final has a usable wide promotional framing of the hall and courtyard.
issues: Materials are largely glossy or flat synthetic surfaces, reducing the feel of stone, aged wood, tiled roofing, and carved guardians.
The guardians and shrub/tree forms are visibly primitive and repetitive.
Large portions beneath roofs and around the side buildings collapse into near-black shadow.
The courtyard sits against a sparse black-to-olive void, so it does not feel like a fully situated old-town environment.

dimensions.reasons: The requested spatial hierarchy is clear: the straight gray-blue stone-paved path leads from the foreground entrance toward the central hall stairs; two guardian figures flank the entry in the author final; the bronze object is centered before the hall; and the lantern rack is placed on the right side of the court. Group A elevated views confirm a sensible courtyard arrangement with a pavilion at left and trees/side structures at right.
issues: The frontal author-final composition weakens the requested angled-in gateway viewpoint.
The left pavilion occupies a large portion of the foreground and competes with the main hall from some viewpoints.
The bell/cauldron is placed centrally rather than reading as a prominent landmark or corner feature.

dimensions.reasons: The main hall, raised porch, columns, stairs, pavilion, paving, lantern rack, and surrounding walls have mostly sensible relative sizes in the Group A elevated views. The central axial route is comfortably scaled for a courtyard.
issues: The foreground guardian figures appear oversized and bulky relative to the path and pavilion columns.
The supposedly big bronze bell is comparatively small and visually slight against the hall.
The spherical tree crowns and cone evergreens feel simplified and somewhat toy-like relative to the architecture.

dimensions.reasons: The author final uses warm directional dusk-like illumination, producing readable highlights on the gold-brown roofs, red columns, stone paving, and bronze-colored central object. Stone steps and paving have more material variation than the simpler painted architectural surfaces.
issues: The lighting is harshly contrasty, with very dark eaves, side corridors, and foreground recesses obscuring detail.
Lanterns do not appear to cast or contribute visible warm light.
Roof, wall, and wood surfaces read mostly as uniformly glossy/plastic rather than distinct traditional materials.
The empty black-to-olive surrounding background reduces the warm, quaint dusk atmosphere.

dimensions.reasons: The main hall, red columns, golden swept roof, straight paved path, pair of entry-side guardian forms, side pavilion, trees, planters, central bronze object, and multiple hanging lanterns are all visibly included. The right-side lantern rack clearly supplies the requested corner lantern grouping.
issues: The central bronze object is not visibly a bell; it reads as an incense burner or bowl on a stand.
The two requested stone lions are present as symmetric forms but are too amorphous to be reliably recognized as lions.
Lanterns are pink rather than red.
The surrounding old-town/courtyard enclosure remains sparse and underdeveloped beyond the immediate architectural props.

criteria.criterion: The delivered final image is a finished, characterful, quaint, and elegant promotional depiction of a traditional Chinese temple courtyard.
criteria.evidence: The designated authored final image, temple_courtyard_dusk.png, is a complete composed render showing a roofed traditional East Asian hall, paved courtyard, side pavilion, lantern frame, landscaping, and entry statues. The organized axial composition and recurring red-and-gold architectural treatment read clearly as a stylized traditional temple court.

criteria.criterion: The principal main hall combines visual dominance, red columns, and a golden traditional upturned-eave roof.
criteria.evidence: The large central two-storey hall is the dominant subject in cam_submitted.png and temple_courtyard_dusk.png. It has a prominent row of glossy red columns and two substantial gold-brown tiled roofs with strongly curled, lifted corners.

criteria.criterion: Two recognizable carved-stone guardian lions form a paired installation at the gateway.
criteria.evidence: Although two symmetric gray-brown pedestal figures appear at the front of temple_courtyard_dusk.png, their forms are assembled from indistinct intersecting rounded lumps and blocks. Neither statue has a clearly recognizable guardian-lion silhouette or carved-lion detail.

criteria.criterion: The open courtyard, straight bluestone route to the hall, and relative orientation of all major elements form a clearly readable layout.
criteria.evidence: temple_courtyard_dusk.png clearly presents an open paved court with a straight central cool gray brick/bluestone-like route bordered by pale raised strips, running from the entry-statue foreground to the hall stairs. The right lantern frame and axial hall remain spatially legible, and wide_elevated.png confirms the open courtyard arrangement.

criteria.criterion: A defined courtyard corner contains the complete large bronze-bell and plausibly suspended red-lantern vignette.
criteria.evidence: The right-side wooden frame visibly suspends several pink lanterns, but the only bronze-colored object is centered on the main path before the hall. In detail_lions.png and wide_gateway.png it reads as a bowl-like burner/vessel on legs rather than a recognizable large temple bell, and it is not part of the lantern corner vignette.

criteria.criterion: The final image combines a recognizable warm dusk atmosphere with bright, readable courtyard detail.
criteria.evidence: The authored final image uses warm amber illumination across the gold roofs, red columns, stone paving, and lanterns against a muted gray-green dusk sky. Despite strong directional shadows, the hall, central route, statues, lantern frame, and courtyard paving remain visibly readable.

criteria.criterion: The usable native project contains the complete authored scene and implements the requested inward-angled gateway camera view.

notes: The submission successfully communicates a stylized Chinese temple courtyard centered on a recognizable red-and-gold main hall, with a clear axial path and supporting pavilion/lantern layout. Its largest failures are the unreadable guardian lions, the cauldron-like object substituted for a bronze bell, overly dark peripheral spaces, and a centered rather than angled gateway composition.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
